div.p: Correspondence about the publication date of Vigrinia Woolf's novel: Flush. Donald Brace informs that he will choose the same publication date for Flush - October 5th. He requests 2 copies of Woolf's editions for copyright purposes and has enclosed a letter from the Atlantic Monthly. Typescript letter signed by Brace [enclosure not present at the time of cataloguing].

address.addrLine:
c/o The Hogarth Press
The Hogarth Press was a British publishing house founded by Leonard Woolf and his wife Virginia Woolf.

opener.salute:
Dear Mr.Mister Woolf:
Leonard Woolf was a British political theorist, author, publisher, and civil servant. He was married to author Virginia Woolf.

div.p:
I am delighted to hear that the Book Society
The first British monthly book sales club, modelled on the American Book-of-the-Month Club.is taking FLUSH
Flush: A Biography, is an imaginative biography of Elizabeth Barrett Browning (poet of the Victorian era)'s cocker spaniel, written by Virginia Woolf and published in 1933.as their October selection. The changes in your plans need not, I think, affect us at all. We were already making a larger book than you were, and we shall go ahead with Mrs.Missus Bell’s drawings as end papers and with the three photo- graphs we already have.
Vanessa Bell, was an English painter and interior designer, and the older sister of Virginia Woolf, she designed the endpapers for Virginia's book FLUSH.

I note that your publication date will now be October fifth. We shall choose the same date unless something, perhaps a book club choice here, should make a change necessary. In any event, of course our date couldn’t be before October fifth. The Book-of-the-Month Club
American bookclub, founded in 1926. is definitely interested, but as three of their judges are in Europe, it will be some little time before we shall have their final decision.
I wish you would send me two copies of your edition when you have it ready so that we may be in a position to use them, if we need to, for copyrighting purposes.
We shall be glad to send you £20 as our fee for the use of Mrs.Missus Bell’s end papers.

Thank you for cabling so promptly the corrections in respect to the dates in FLUSH. I don’t know whether the Atlantic
American literary and cultural magazine, and publisher.will have time to correct all of them or not, but of course we are correcting them in the book.
See enclosed letter from the Atlantic just received.
